string.name: discover_guide_entry
string.value: No server on your computer yet? View the setup guide

string.name: guide_step1_title
string.value: Step 1 · Open the download page on your computer

string.name: guide_step1_body
string.value: Type this address into your computer's browser:

string.name: guide_step1_hint
string.value: Copy the one-line install command near the top of the page and run it in a terminal on your computer, or follow the manual steps below.

string.name: guide_step2_title
string.value: Step 2 · Install and start on your computer

string.name: guide_ubuntu_s1
string.value: 1. Download padlink_<version>_linux_amd64.deb, then in the download folder run:

string.name: guide_ubuntu_s2
string.value: 2. Log out and back in (required on first install for input injection to work)

string.name: guide_ubuntu_s3
string.value: 3. Start the server and enable autostart:

string.name: guide_macos_s1
string.value: 1. Download padlink_<version>_darwin_arm64.tar.gz (amd64 for Intel) and extract it

string.name: guide_macos_s3
string.value: 3. On first run, allow both prompts: Accessibility and Incoming connections

string.name: guide_step3_body
string.value: Once installed, the server runs in the background. Go back to the discovery page, tap Rescan, then tap the host that appears to pair. The 4-digit code shows as a desktop notification on the computer (or run padlinkctl pair in a terminal).

string.name: guide_trouble_title
string.value: Installed but still not showing up?

string.name: guide_trouble_1
string.value: · Phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi; disable AP isolation / client isolation on the router

string.name: guide_trouble_2
string.value: · Allow UDP/TCP port 53021 through the computer's firewall

string.name: guide_trouble_3
string.value: · On Ubuntu, log out and back in once after the first install

string.name: guide_trouble_4
string.value: · Run padlinkctl status on the computer — it must print a version number
